findings.reason: The protected source repeatedly uses the campaign-forbidden generic local name index for both the dynamic-programming position and the reconstruction cursor, and next_index obscures that the array stores chosen successors. The candidate distinguishes position, successor, and candidate_cost without changing any decision or data flow; normalized AST comparison confirms those semantic renames are its only changes.

The inert candidate preserves the Accepted right-to-left cost DP and strict-improvement tie rule while making each coordinate and transition role explicit. It retains the exact solve(coins, maxJump) contract, control structure, asymptotic bounds, and reconstruction behavior, with no extra helpers or algorithmic variation.

The destination is seeded with its own cost when unblocked. Processing positions right to left ensures every reachable following suffix is already optimal; checking every landing position through maxJump therefore finds the minimum suffix cost. Following positions are scanned increasingly and a successor is replaced only for a strictly lower cost, so equal-cost choices keep the smaller next one-based position and hence the lexicographically smaller full path. Infinite start cost yields an empty result, while following successor from a finite start reconstructs exactly the chosen path.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 656, Python, and the native cheapestJump(coins, maxJump) interface. The candidate preserves nonnegative visit costs, -1 blocked positions, forward jumps of at most maxJump, inclusion of both endpoint costs, one-based output, empty unreachable output, and lexicographic minimization among minimum-cost paths.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065525290 use the same reverse order, cost and successor arrays, blocked-position skip, bounded following-position scan, strict cost improvement, reachability test, and pointer reconstruction. The candidate changes only semantic local names, remains inert, and does not replace or alter that Accepted evidence.

The recalibrated legal workloads grow a unique zero-cost unit-jump path from 25 to 1000 positions, so one reverse topological pass scales linearly while a correct repeated-relaxation DP with a linearly growing pass count revisits the same states quadratically. The exact candidate passed all 10 correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent -0.00 and a 0.99x largest runtime ratio. The terminating repeated-relaxation control passed every correctness and benchmark output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +0.46 and a 5.85x largest runtime ratio. The former tiers were rejected because a natural quadratic path-copy control passed scaling and an unbounded repeated-relaxation control hit the safety cap instead of reaching the verdict.

The candidate-targeted Approach now precisely describes the minimum suffix cost, increasing following-position scan, strict-improvement lexicographic rule, `successor` reconstruction, and blocked or unreachable states. Its O(N * B) time and O(N) auxiliary-space claims match the candidate and branch manifest.

The modular Reference preserves the 1-indexed array model, blocked-position rule, visit costs, bounded forward jumps, guaranteed valid start, minimum-cost objective, one-based output, unreachable result, and the source's complete lexicographic comparison definition. It presents exactly the two source examples without invented explanations and records all four constraints.

Authenticated Premium evidence established the four-paragraph statement structure, exact lexicographic-order definition, exactly two examples without explanations, and the four constraints: 1 <= coins.length <= 1000, -1 <= coins[i] <= 100, coins[1] != -1, and 1 <= maxJump <= 100. It also confirmed that there are no notes, hints, tables, visuals, or follow-up. The modular files are hash-bound in a verified source_fidelity.json to live description hash 4c4dc84b6d4c55a2cbe6aabdd5be71898320316eef611ea20b4435a58dbe0efd.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly two examples. Their exact coins, maxJump, and output facts now appear first and in source order; the invented four-one tie example was relabelled as a trial rather than presented as a third source sample.

All ordinary correctness checks are visible samples or trials. The former hidden blocked-start check was removed because the source guarantees the first position is unblocked, while the two legal hidden checks were retained and exposed as trials.

Contract boundaries cover one and 1000 positions, maxJump values one and 100, visit costs zero and 100, blocked positions at -1, a valid first position, and a blocked destination. The maximum-size case returns immediately and therefore remains correctness-only rather than a performance workload.

Material semantics cover an obstacle gap wider than maxJump, zero-cost ties that retain earlier indices, equal positive-cost suffixes, tie resolution around an obstacle, minimum cost outweighing a shorter path, one-based reconstruction, and unreachable output.

Expected results were checked against an independent complete-path enumerator and a tuple-based dynamic-programming oracle across 109,227 exhaustive legal small inputs and 500 seeded random legal inputs, as well as all authored cases and benchmarks. The protected app/native forms and the inert naming candidate agreed throughout.

All ten ordinary cases are visible. The recalibrated 25, 200, and 1000-position zero-cost unit-jump workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, span 40x, and make the terminating correct repeated-relaxation control fail only the scaling verdict without reaching the safety cap.
